rows.what the ink shows: Between que and the formula, an angular open loop and one upright survive below two broad cancelling strokes; the remaining baseline joins are merged with the deletion and do not identify a word.

The first symbol has a rounded lower bowl and a right exit stroke; next is the curved membership sign with its middle arm, followed by a tall E with three horizontal arms. The cancellation crosses their upper parts without hiding these distinctions.

A short initial curved remnant, isolated uprights and a dot survive along the upper deleted word, but the heavy horizontal cancellation absorbs most letter bodies and the accent area; the full sequence considérant cannot be resolved.

The lower deleted line retains a low initial bend, several uprights and short descenders, ending in a downward hook. Its continuous thick cancellation hides the proposed le and vecteur letter joins and their division.

The first deleted word begins with several tall connected strokes; later an open rounded capital, small low remnants and a looped descender remain. Most intervening letters lie directly under the cancellation, so the full proposed sentence remains uncertain.

The left number has a distinct 1 and the upper bar and bend of 5 within parentheses. The following open capital, small a-like bowl and later descender support the proposed words, but the cancellation conceals their intervening letter bodies.

The shared deleted fragment starts with a large open curved letter, followed by compressed baseline ink and a small dark lobe; two long cancellation strokes hide the distinguishing middle letters. A terminal looped a survives farther right, but its allocation between this mark and following M1018 cannot be established.

The upper deleted fragment has two long cancellation strokes, a large opening curve and a terminal looped a. No separate word boundary for this illegible span can be recovered from the intervening covered baseline; its boundary with M1017 remains unresolved.

On the lower deleted line a small round mark and detached mark survive at the left, with tangled upright/looped ink farther right; cancellation conceals the first words. The following upright l, low s-led run and terminal d remain visible as le second.
After second there is one compressed low m stroke followed by a short upright b with a foot, then the comma. There is no following re sequence to support the expanded membre.
The deleted short word has a tall looped l followed by a small low e, both crossed by the heavy horizontal cancellation.
The word has the tall t near its middle and continues with a low e/r run to a distinct terminal a-like arch; it extends beyond the shorter reste ending.
Between the two u forms the arrow has a plain left end and a right-pointing terminal hook. There is no vertical stem at the left end for mapsto.
A separate overbar sits above the three-stroke E. Immediately afterward is the round tensor sign, crossed by the cancellation; the space before norme contains no additional baseline letter.
A small closed ascender-loop supports initial d. The remaining short bodies lie under a thick horizontal cancellation, which prevents distinguishing e and s separately.

One tall narrow loop continues below the cancellation into a rightward lower hook, supporting baseline l. A separate smaller upper-right mark has a curved cap and descending bend like the visible 2 in Définition 2; the long deletion line runs left from the letter, with no other distinct baseline letter exposed.

A dot above the middle, a small loop farther right, and the final upright/crossing stroke survive. The continuous heavy deletion hides the initial and several connecting letter bodies, so the full proposed word cannot be recovered securely.
The single capital has an open right side, an upper curved arm and a distinct inward middle arm; its lower arm remains visible through the short cancellation.
Two uprights and some rounded connecting strokes survive under several overlapping cancellation lines. The middle and terminal bodies are too merged to identify the complete word toutes securely.
The cancellation crosses a small initial loop, a separate rounded middle shoulder and a final upright t with its foot; these three bodies support est.
